## b24eadbaf79d

**Disposition: reproduced distribution shortcut and override-contract defects; target left unchanged.** Audited generator SHA-256: `42bc82b9233151529fb4b520d2eb1e102f18ecb3b9fe2a26a4055e76c7934bc0`.

Across 300 pinned generated samples (100 per easy/medium/hard), the marker was below the template in 300/300 and above it in 0/300. Canonical train pair 1 contains the opposite lawful orientation: marker row 1, template rows 4–6. A solver can therefore learn “copy only downward from a marker above the template” from generated data and fail a canonical case while still matching the generator distribution.

The same source-bound probe reproduced four control defects at seed 314159, sample index 7, medium difficulty: `variant=a` and `variant=b` are byte-identical; default palette and `palette_kind=cool` are byte-identical; declared `grid_h=9` yields height 11; and an unknown override is accepted. These are contract defects rather than merely low-frequency observations.

Reproducer: `checks/audit/b24eadbaf79d/reproduce_orientation_and_axes.py`. Results, including the canonical counterexample: `checks/audit/b24eadbaf79d/orientation_and_axes.json`. Official rule smoke passes, so this audit does not allege a wrong rule implementation; lint/override/defect checks expose the metadata and dead-control issues under `checks/audit/b24eadbaf79d/`; the completed defect-lint replay is in `checks/audit/b24eadbaf79d/defect-lint-final/`.
